scenario.title: Machine admission, shared capacity and retirement
situations: Make a machine available to other operators.
Retire or reconnect a machine after credentials change.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Does machine retirement explain effects on running sessions and outstanding custody?
Where is capacity sharing taught before users encounter a placement refusal?

lessons.title: Approve the right machine and identity
lessons.when: Connecting another computer or recovering an expired device code
lessons.need: Read the actual server sign-in method, code identity and origin. Own-machine self-host approval binds the approver; do not approve a teammate code as if it were yours. Pending, expired, denied and consumed have different continuation rules.
lessons.surface: Install/Actors guide -> machine authorization reference -> connect/get help.

lessons.title: Sharing capacity has its own access policy
lessons.when: A teammate should be able to run workers on this machine
lessons.need: Machine access.use controls owner-only, selected actors, project-role or universe use. The offers block is reserved and is not enforced for placement, deploys or QA; never treat its presence as a restriction.
lessons.surface: Machine register/settings help and source contract expose the policy; natural discovery from the dashboard or launch blocker was not traced.
lessons.gap: This is an implemented contract with an untraced human/agent entry cue, not absent support.

lessons.title: Retirement differs from disconnecting a shell
lessons.when: Removing a machine from the usable fleet
lessons.need: Inspect the machine and ownership before retirement; understand retained history and affected credentials/capacity. Read operation help rather than assuming uninstall or stopping a relay retires the registry row.
lessons.surface: Machine list/show/detail/retire registered adapter; deeper end-to-end retirement not traced.
